title: Regular grants
amount_raw: Our grants range from £1,000 to several million pounds, depending on each charity's size and scope of work
eligibility_summary: UK registered charities across welfare, youth, community, environment, education, health, arts, heritage and faith. Organisations must have filed accounts, and annual income under £5,000 is discouraged. Universities, schools and colleges may apply for CAPITAL developments or discrete projects outside formal education activity, but NOT for operating/core costs; a university application requires a covering letter from the Pro/Vice Chancellor and only one application per institution may be live at a time. The Foundation is not a specialist research or medical funder — medical research is supported only from major specialist organisations with international peer review.
summary: The Foundation's main, always-open grants programme, made in three forms: capital projects (building works, repairs, necessary equipment), operating/core costs, and projects/specific activity. Applications are submitted through an online portal at any time and reviewed in the order received, with a decision aimed at within 4-6 months.
notes: ROLLING call: no deadline appears anywhere in the mirror, and the application FAQs confirm a continuous process ('We review applications in the order we receive them ... we will aim to get back to you with our decision within 4-6 months'), so deadlines is empty per the protocol. title is FLAGGED — the Foundation gives this programme no heading of its own; 'Regular grants' is the site's own contrastive term, taken from the Major Grants page ('we advise you apply for a regular grant via our online portal'). The three grant types (capital / operating-core / projects) are recorded as ONE row rather than three because they share a single application form, a single portal and a single set of criteria, and no per-type cap is published — contrast the Henry Moore categories, which have distinct caps. amount_max_gbp flagged: the stated range tops out at 'several million pounds' with no figure, and separately local community capital projects (church, village hall) are typically capped at £30,000. RESEARCHER-AUDIENCE CAVEAT / FLAG FOR REVIEW: this is a general charity funder, not a research funder, so the inclusion rule's 'available to some UK-based researchers' clause is satisfied only indirectly — universities are eligible for capital and non-teaching project costs, which is the basis for in_scope=yes here.

title: Major Grants
eligibility_summary: The total cost of what is being applied for must be at least £1 million. For core costs, the organisation's annual income must be £1 million or over; for capital or project costs the organisation's income need not exceed £1 million but the total project cost must. Local community capital projects (churches, village halls) are directed to the regular grants route instead, where the typical maximum is £30,000. Same charity eligibility as the regular programme.
summary: The Foundation's route for requests of £100,000 and above: an Expression of Interest form submitted through the Grants Management Portal, answered with bespoke guidance within 10 working days, followed by a call if the request is potentially suitable.
notes: ROLLING: an Expression of Interest may be submitted at any time; no deadline or round appears on the page, so deadlines is empty. Recorded as a SEPARATE row from the regular grants rather than folded in, because it has a distinct application route (EOI rather than full application), a distinct threshold (£100,000+) and its own eligibility test (total project cost of at least £1 million) — the material facts differ. FLAG FOR REVIEW if the reviewer prefers a single Garfield Weston row. amount_max_gbp flagged: no ceiling is published, only the £100,000 floor.

title: Weston Charity Awards
amount_raw: a package of support worth over £22,000, including unrestricted grants of £6,500
eligibility_summary: Registered charities working with beneficiaries in the North of England, the Midlands and Wales, specialising in Community, Welfare, Youth or Environment, with at least one paid full-time member of staff in a leadership position and annual income under £5 million.
summary: An annual award run with Pilotlight: an unrestricted £6,500 grant plus ten months of pro-bono coaching from senior private and public sector professionals (valued at about £16,000).
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the round described closed at '5pm on Wednesday 8th January 2025', over nineteen months before the 2026-08-16 snapshot, and no page in the mirror announces a subsequent round or a future opening date.
notes: A prime distractor: the page headline reads 'Applications are now open for the annual Weston Charity Awards!' and it is the only Garfield Weston page in the mirror that announces an open call with a deadline — but it is dated 5 November 2024 and its deadline is long past. An extractor keying on 'applications are now open' will report this wrongly. The scheme is described as annual, which implies further rounds, but no date for one is given, so it stays excluded rather than forthcoming. Geographically restricted (North of England, Midlands, Wales).

title: Weston Loan Programme with Art Fund
amount_raw: Over £300,000 has been awarded in this round, bringing the total so far to almost £1.6 million across 93 organisations since the scheme began in 2017
eligibility_summary: Smaller regional museums, galleries and historic buildings across the UK borrowing major works from national or major lending museums. The programme is run by Art Fund, not by the Foundation.
summary: The first UK-wide grant programme designed to fund smaller museums to borrow major works from national lending institutions such as Tate, the National Portrait Gallery, the British Library and the British Museum.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule as an informational page: it announces the RESULTS of a completed round ('Twelve regional galleries and museums ... have been awarded grants'), gives no deadline, no application route and no future opening date. Applications are in any case made to Art Fund rather than to the Foundation.
notes: Distractor. Dated 27 March 2024. A second, near-identical announcement page for the tenth round (about-us/news-insights/tenth-round-of-weston-loan-programme-with-art-fund-announced) is also in the mirror and is NOT given its own row — one row per scheme per the canonical rule, with the other location noted here. The £300,000 figure is the round total across twelve recipients, not a per-grant value, so amount_min_gbp and amount_max_gbp are left blank and flagged.

title: Weston Culture Fund
amount_raw: granting a total of £30.2 million in 106 grants
eligibility_summary: Cultural organisations that lost significant earned income due to Covid-19 closures. Applications are no longer invited.
summary: A one-off 2020 fund to help cultural organisations emerge from the pandemic; £128 million was requested and £30.2 million awarded in 106 grants, with an external evaluation published in 2022.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule as an informational page: it is an evaluation report of a fund launched in 2020 and long since closed, with no deadline, no application route and no future opening date.
notes: Distractor. Dated 1 March 2022 and filed under Research Reports rather than as a funding page — but it names a large fund and a large sum, so an agent scanning for '£' and 'Fund' could surface it. £30.2 million is the whole programme's spend across 106 grants, not a per-grant value, hence blank and flagged amount bounds.
